title: Dynamics of communication on measles vaccination on digital platforms in the Brazilian context: challenges and perspectives
screen_reason: Deductive qualitative content analysis of Brazilian Portuguese Facebook posts about measles vaccination. Table 3 ('Posts with disinformation') gives explicit counts and percentages with denominators for two separate corpora: 6/252 (2.4%) of posts drawn from general pages by keyword search, and 115/173 (66.5%) of posts from a public anti-vaccine group. Both are CONTENT prevalence estimates with an explicit disinformation code.

estimates.measure_type: % of analysed Brazilian Portuguese Facebook posts about measles vaccines (retrieved by keyword search on general pages) that contained disinformation
estimates.value_raw: Disinformation Yes: n = 6, 2.4%; No: n = 246, 97.6%; Total 252 (Table 3, keyword search column)
estimates.denominator: 252 Facebook posts selected for deductive qualitative analysis from general public pages, drawn from 117,662 posts across 19,377 pages containing the keywords 'Measles Vaccine', 'Triple Viral' and 'Tetra Viral', restricted to posts with a CrowdTangle performance score of zero or above
estimates.definition: A post was coded 'disinformation: yes' under the codebook category 'presence of disinformation'; such posts "often misrepresented scientific studies, media reports, and case reports of alleged vaccine-related adverse events", with conspiracy theories targeting health institutions, governments, the media and the pharmaceutical industry
estimates.misinfo_def: No formal definition given; the codebook category is 'presence of disinformation' (codebook in Supplementary File S1, not reproduced in the text), operationalised through misrepresentation of scientific studies, media reports and adverse-event case reports, and conspiracy theories
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Deductive content analysis in ATLAS.ti (v23.1.2) against a seven-category codebook (Supplementary File S1) that includes 'presence of disinformation'. No inter-coder reliability statistic, no number of coders and no adjudication procedure are reported anywhere in the paper.
estimates.moderator_quote: For this analysis, only posts with a performance score equal to or greater than zero were included. Posts with low performance (score less than or equal to zero) were excluded. The CrowdTangle tool provides this performance metric, in which a post is considered over-performing when it surpasses a benchmark based on interactions (likes, shares, comments, and link clicks) as compared to expected metrics.
estimates.notes: 6/252 = 2.4%, exactly as in Table 3. denom_selection=curated: the 252 analysed posts are not a random sample of the 117,662 keyword-matching posts; they were filtered to over-performing posts and selected 'based on the criteria outlined in Figure 1', a flowchart whose contents are not reproduced in the text, so the selection cannot be fully reconstructed. This is the general-population-facing estimate of the two and the one comparable to other keyword-corpus prevalence figures. year=2020 is the last year of the collection window (2017-2020); the paper does not report a single reference year.

estimates.measure_type: % of analysed posts from one public Brazilian anti-vaccine Facebook group ('O Lado Obscuro das Vacinas') that contained disinformation
estimates.value_raw: Disinformation Yes: n = 115, 66.5%; No: n = 58, 33.5%; Total 173 (Table 3, antivaccine page column)
estimates.denominator: 173 posts selected for deductive qualitative analysis from the public anti-vaccine Facebook group 'O Lado Obscuro das Vacinas' (The Dark Side of Vaccines), which had 14,901 members and had published 5,489 posts (7,770 posts extracted) between 28 December 2014 and 1 May 2021
estimates.definition: A post was coded 'disinformation: yes' under the codebook category 'presence of disinformation'; on this page such posts typically undermined vaccine safety and efficacy, citing associations with autism, neurological disease and weakened immunity from aluminium and mercury/thimerosal
estimates.misinfo_def: No formal definition given; the codebook category is 'presence of disinformation', operationalised through misrepresentation of scientific studies, media reports and adverse-event case reports, and conspiracy theories
estimates.source_quote: Disinformation was identified in 66.5% of posts on
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Same deductive codebook analysis in ATLAS.ti; no inter-coder reliability, coder count or adjudication procedure reported.
estimates.moderator_quote: The second dataset targeted a public anti-vaccine Facebook® group titled O Lado Obscuro das Vacinas (The Dark side of Vaccines), consisting of 14,901 members when the data were extracted (December 2014 to May 2021).
estimates.notes: 115/173 = 66.5%, exactly as in Table 3. JUDGEMENT CALL: borderline=true and denom_selection=single_source because the denominator is one purposively chosen anti-vaccine group, so 66.5% is the falsity rate inside a source selected for being anti-vaccine, not a prevalence estimate for Brazilian Facebook. I did NOT set within_misinfo_content=true because the group is defined by stance, not by verified falsity (its own sentiment breakdown is 78.6% anti-vaccine/hesitant, 20.2% neutral, 1.2% pro-vaccine), but an adjudicator who reads R3 more broadly could reasonably flag it that way and confine it to the appendix. year=2021 is the last year of the collection window (2014-2021).

missed_or_uncertain: (1) The sentiment analysis (Table 2: keyword search 84.5% pro-vaccine, 12.7% neutral, 2.8% anti-vaccine/hesitant; anti-vaccine page 1.2% / 20.2% / 78.6%) measures stance, not veracity, so it is not a misinformation prevalence share and was not extracted. (2) The 'context of posts' arguments' table (Table 4: vaccine safety and efficacy 38.9% / 59.3%, conspiracy theory 0.8% / 13.6%, civil liberty 0.8% / 11.6%, etc.) codes argument topic, not falsity, and its anti-vaccine column sums to 199 codes over 173 posts because posts could receive several codes, so no clean denominator exists. The 59.3% quoted in the abstract is this argument-topic share, not a disinformation share. (3) The determinants-of-hesitancy table (Table 5) and the resource-type shares (39.3% text, 60.7% images) describe form and framing, not veracity. (4) Comment-level shares (443/659 = 67.2% of pro-vaccine comments promoted vaccination; 108/142 = 76.1% of comments on anti-vaccine posts expressed anti-vaccine sentiment or hesitancy) are stance codes on comments, not disinformation codes, so they are not prevalence rows. (5) Engagement counts in Table 1 (2,735,420 total interactions across the top 20 pages) have no misinformation denominator and cannot be turned into an exposure-weighted estimate. (6) '8,427 cases of measles' and 'vaccination rates declining by 10% to 20% since 2016' are epidemiological background figures cited from the Ministry of Health, not misinformation measures. (7) 'Approximately 5% of all internet searches pertain to health topics' is cited from elsewhere.

rob.design: Qualitative deductive content analysis of two Facebook corpora extracted with CrowdTangle (public pages and groups only; private groups inaccessible). Corpus A: 117,662 posts across 19,377 pages matching 'Measles Vaccine', 'Triple Viral', 'Tetra Viral' in Brazilian Portuguese, 1 January 2017 - 31 December 2020, from which 252 posts were selected for coding after excluding posts with a CrowdTangle performance score at or below zero and applying unstated criteria in the Figure 1 flowchart. Corpus B: 7,770 posts extracted from one public anti-vaccine group (14,901 members), 28 December 2014 - 1 May 2021, from which 173 were coded. Comments (801) extracted with Export Comments, capped at 100 comments per post in the free version. Coding done in ATLAS.ti against a seven-category codebook in Supplementary File S1. NO inter-coder reliability, no coder count, no adjudication rule, and no sampling probability for the coded subsets are reported: the selection from 117,662 posts down to 252 is the weakest link. Single-platform, single-country, single-language design; the authors note the anti-vaccine page was removed from Facebook in 2022, limiting comment extraction.
rob.item6_quote: Second, a qualitative analysis of the posts was conducted using seven categories: (a) type of pages, (b) page description (vaccine or non-vaccine-specific content), (c) sentiment analysis, (d) presence of disinformation, (e) context of the post, (f) determinants of vaccine hesitancy, and (g) types of resources used.
